primary_claim: Across independent North American and Australian acoustic monitoring systems, more recent rainfall is associated with greater short-window overlap in frog calling activity across species.
interpretation: shared environmental activation is consistent with transient compression of temporal separation among calling species at the observation-window scale

FrogID.design: expert-validated short call recordings conditional on >=1 calling species

prior_art_boundary: Rainfall-triggered frog calling, calling-species richness, and chorus-onset synchrony are established in prior work; novelty is short-window multispecies co-calling overlap, conditional FrogID validation, independent continental replication, and prospective cross-system analysis.

temperature.interpretation_authorized: warmer conditions are associated with greater event-level multispecies calling overlap in NAAMP after documented plausibility/source-scale checks and flexible day-of-year adjustment

prohibited: first-ever rainfall synchronization of frog choruses
direct meta-analysis of NAAMP and FrogID odds ratios
claim that all spatial or temporal confounding is eliminated
